correctness.rationale: Independent recomputation from stored multiplication tables confirms every headline number. G1 table (168 elements): inverses ok, 2000-sample associativity ok, orders verified (1:1,2:21,3:56,4:42,7:48). G2 table (504): same checks pass; MT matches F8 matrix multiplication on random samples and all dets=1. Order-filtered enumeration gives N1=336 and N2=1512 exactly, with z-class fibers 168+168 (G1) and 504+504+504 (G2). Pure-braid BFS (s1^2,s2^2 and inverses, with xyz=1 and closure asserts) gives 2x168 for G1 and 3x504 for G2; z-class constant on each orbit and distinct across orbits. Full-braid BFS on pattern-union gives |U1|=2016 in 2x1008 and |U2|=9072 in 3x3024. Simultaneous-conjugation reduction gives 2 Inn-classes of 168 (G1) and 3 of 504 (G2). Exhaustive subgroup-closure generation checked for ALL pairs: 0 failures among 336 (G1) and 1512 (G2); 20-sample spot checks plus full runs both pass. Dickson-Lagrange exclusion argument is arithmetically sound (G1: 7 does not divide 24 excludes S4, 2 does not divide 21 excludes F21; G2: 7 does not divide 18 excludes D18, 3 does not divide 14 excludes D14, 3 does not divide 56 excludes F56) and is redundant with the exhaustive closure check, so completeness of ATLAS maximal lists is not load-bearing. F8 commutator traces recomputed from stored F8 matrix lifts with explicit F8 arithmetic (mod 0xB): reps give traces 2,6,4 matching claimed values; G1 SL-lift trace 3 on both orbits confirmed as stated. This is computational certification (exhaustive enumeration over at most |G|^2=28224/254016 pairs plus BFS), not an abstract proof, and is honestly presented as such with a replay script.

value.rationale: TARGET route: exact (2,3,7) braid-orbit/component counts for the closed initial segment of Hurwitz PSL(2,q) groups by order (168,504) with joining words and a defining-characteristic separator. Braid orbits = Hurwitz-space components = Galois orbits of regular dessins/Macbeath-Hurwitz maps is a recognized frontier since Hurwitz/Macbeath/Fried-Voelklein/Conder, with flagship downstream objects Klein quartic (genus 3) and Fricke-Macbeath curve (genus 7). The object and invariant were motivated before computation, the b-counts are not known or mechanically implied by characters/ATLAS (which give at most N), and a future researcher needs the precise component degrees (168/168; 504/504/504, reduced degrees 2 and 3). This is a rigorously established exact invariant of a specific natural object, eligible under the narrow-datum policy; it is not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny gain, or unexplained enumeration.
